stops.name: Ascona, Castello San Materno
stops.campa: Paul Bachrach, who first saw the lake of Locarno on a holiday in 1910 and never forgot it, buys the Castello San Materno above Ascona, once a summer house of the canons of Milan cathedral, and sets the architect Paul Rudolf Henning to enlarge it. In 1920 the family settles for good. Charlotte writes north to Vogeler of the magnolias and amaryllis flowering at her new door. In the castle's great hall she begins at once to dance for invited guests: the castle is her first theater.

stops.name: Monte Verità, the inherited mountain
stops.campa: Above her castle rises Monte Verità, the mountain of truth, where the life-reformers went barefoot and Rudolf Laban kept his dance farm in the summers before the war. By the time Charlotte climbs it the magus is gone north; she never stands in his studio, and the canon keeps the distinction clean. Yet the hill and the dancer belong to one story: his line will reach her by descent through Wigman's pupils in Berlin, and Ascona now has, in the castle below the hill, a second consecrated body.

stops.name: Locarno: the Kursaal, first Ticino recital
stops.campa: Her first appearance before her new countrymen: an evening at the Teatro Kursaal in Locarno, dancing to Chopin, Grieg and Granados. The Ticinese, who know the Ascona hill mostly as a rumor of vegetarians and anarchists, discover instead a grave young woman performing the attitudes of their own church porches: adoration, lamentation, the folded hands of the stone Madonnas. The region adopts her; for the next thirty-six years the shore between Locarno and Ascona is her parish.

stops.name: Berlin, Cürlis turns the camera
stops.campa: At the Institut für Kulturforschung in Berlin, Hans Cürlis, pioneer of the culture-film, sets his camera before her and records twelve minutes of the gothic dances. It is among the earliest attempts to give the new dance a body that outlives the evening. The film is later lost: the fate the canon assigns to almost everything she made, an art of attitudes surviving only in bronze, drawings and print. The dancer who took her grammar from things that last a thousand years leaves moving images that last thirty.

stops.name: Locarno, the Festa delle Camelie
stops.campa: At the camellia festival of Locarno she gives her first mimed spectacle for the region: Il trionfo della camelia, verses by Silvio Sganzini, scenes and costume by Alexandre Cingria, Leo Kok at the piano. Before the assembled lake she performs the blossoming of a camellia: the closed bud, the slow unclenching, the full flower offered and then let fall. It is botany as theology, the resurrection argued by a flower, and the crowd on the lakefront understands it without a word of doctrine.

stops.name: Gardone Riviera, summoned to the Vittoriale
stops.campa: In 1924 Gabriele d'Annunzio, new-made Prince of Montenevoso, calls her to the Vittoriale on Lake Garda, and the gothic dancer performs her Egyptian and Hindu compositions and the dances of the cathedrals for the Comandante among his relics. He is taken above all by her hands, spiritual hands, and names her the santa ballerina, the holy dancer. 'Elle sait par quels mystères surgissent des profondeurs les plus belles clartés,' he writes: she knows by what mysteries the fairest lights rise out of the deepest places.

stops.name: The Vittoriale, the dance invented in a dream
stops.campa: The poet dreams for her. 'J'ai inventé une danse pour vous dans cette nuit en rêve,' he tells her, I invented a dance for you this night, in a dream, and assigns her titles as a poet assigns relics: La dernière colonne du Temple, the last column of the Temple; L'Arbre séraphique et les Oiseaux du ciel, the seraphic tree and the birds of heaven. He intends through her a total sacred artwork, as once with Debussy and Ida Rubinstein: his visions danced, conceivable only on mystical ground.

stops.name: The Vittoriale, Malipiero at the poet's table
stops.campa: Two years on, d'Annunzio summons her again, and at the Vittoriale sets her before Gian Francesco Malipiero, meaning to yoke the composer to the santa ballerina and give the dreamed dances their music. The commission is never realized, the canon's shelf of unbuilt temples receives it, but the meeting bears late fruit: Malipiero's music will carry her Eitelkeit–Vergänglichkeit on the Ascona stage for twenty years. From the lake of the Comandante she returns to her own lake, where her father is preparing the ground of her real temple.

stops.name: Paris, the Comédie des Champs-Élysées
stops.campa: Paris debut at the Comédie des Champs-Élysées, the chamber stage in Perret's concrete temple where the Sacre rioted thirteen years before. The French critics of the dance, Fernand Divoire at their head, take her into the canon of the mystics; Divoire will fix her in Pour la danse among the figures of the age. Paris names what Berlin named, in its own tongue: a dancer not of the theater but of the cathedral, the gothic dancer, sister to the carved saints of the portals.

stops.name: Bad Godesberg, the Rhine seasons
stops.campa: Through 1926 and 1927 she dances at Bad Godesberg on the Rhine, in the Germany of the dance's great ferment. These are working seasons, the recital circuit of spa halls and city theaters by which the soloists of Ausdruckstanz lived, and they set her among her generation: Wigman's ecstatics, Laban's movement choirs, the Sacharoffs' painted legends. Against all of them Bara holds her single note, the sacred attitude, and the note carries. The gothic dancer is now a fixture of the German stage.

stops.name: Berlin, the school of Trümpy and Skoronel
stops.campa: In Berlin she perfects her craft at the school of Berthe Trümpy and Vera Skoronel: Trümpy who was Mary Wigman's pupil and right hand, Skoronel who was Trümpy's. Thus the lineage the canon is careful about: Laban begat Wigman, Wigman begat Trümpy, and through the Trümpy school the magus's method at last touches the gothic dancer, by descent, never by his hand. What Ascona's hill could not give her directly, Berlin gives her at two removes: the discipline of the new dance set beneath her old attitudes.

stops.name: Magdeburg, the First German Dancers' Congress
stops.campa: June 1927: the whole church of the new dance assembles at Magdeburg for the first Deutscher Tänzerkongress, Laban and Wigman at the altar, the schools quarreling like orders of friars, and Charlotte Bara takes part. It is the one documented room that holds her and Laban together: a congress, not a collaboration, and the canon keeps the measure exact. Among the theorists and the ecstatics she stands for the third way of Ausdruckstanz: not the tragic, not the gymnastic, but the liturgical.
